          The 10% Club: Opta's Best Under-the-Radar FPL Picks for Gameweek 8
        
      
                          
                      Oct 21, 2026
          
                      Tom Patey / Author, Emily Millen / Design
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Ready for another instalment of The 10% Club? Well, we’ve got some picks for you ahead of Gameweek 8 in Fantasy Premier League.
The 10% Club enjoyed one of its best returns last weekend. So, why not take note of our Fantasy Premier League picks for Gameweek 8?
With Evanilson (12 points), Luka Vuskovic and Johan Manzambi (both 11) all recording double-digit hauls, three of our five GW7 differentials delivered last time out.
Using Opta data, we’ve got another five under-the-radar gems for the next round of fixtures, and all are in fewer than 10% of squads worldwide.
Ipswich Town may not have kept a clean sheet in 26 Premier League games, but we’re still backing Leif Davis to return when Nottingham Forest visit.
Oliver Glasner’s side are the lowest scorers this season, finding the net just five times. However, Davis is more likely to make a difference in attack rather than banking on a clean sheet.
No defender can beat Davis’ two league goals this campaign, with Maxime De Cuyper and Tyrick Mitchell also twice on target.

Playing out of position on the wing for Brighton, De Cuyper (1.8) is the only defender with a higher expected goals (xG) than Davis’ 1.6. Based on that, chances should continue to flow for our GW8 selection.
The Ipswich full-back is also impressing compared to other budget options. Only Bobby Thomas (31) and Ryan Giles (27) have managed more points than Davis’ 26 among all defenders priced £4m or lower.
Thomas is another tempting pick, but Coventry City have kept just one clean sheet ahead of their meeting with Fulham. Meanwhile, Hull City’s Giles has a tough fixture at home to Brentford.
Davis then visits Hull before a home clash with Bournemouth, and his influence going forward could be key for both Gary O’Neil and prospective FPL managers ahead of the November international break.
Somehow, Leeds United’s defence continues to go under the radar. Only Arsenal and Brighton (five each) have conceded fewer than the six allowed by Daniel Farke’s side.
The 10% Club has already pointed readers towards Tarik Muharemović once, but James Justin is another interesting pick ahead of Leeds’ visit to Sunderland.
Justin scored in his last away game, firing past David Raya at Arsenal and has 34 points in total (Muharemović also has 34). No Leeds defender has had more than his seven shots either.
Jayden Bogle (45) is the only Leeds player with more points this campaign as well, though he has now moved out of reach due to his ownership percentage.

But Justin isn’t just impressing compared to his Leeds teammates. Mentioned last week, Brighton’s Vuskovic (51) is the only player with greater returns than Justin among all FPL defenders owned by fewer than 10% of managers.
Justin, meanwhile, is at least £0.5m cheaper than him and Muharemović. Plus, Sunderland haven’t scored in their last two league games, raising the chances of a Leeds clean sheet.
FPL success is largely about picking players based on either individual form or a promising set of fixtures.

Jack Rudoni falls into the form bracket for Coventry before Fulham travel to the CBS Arena. The midfielder scored from the penalty spot against Newcastle United before equalising against Tottenham last time out.
In doing so, Rudoni became the first player to score in back-to-back Premier League appearances for Coventry since John Hartson netted in four consecutive games between March and April 2001.
